belief: If I looked different, my life would be fine.
origins: It is tempting to believe that one change in our faces, weight, or skin would solve our troubles. The thought supports endless focus on appearance and delays dealing with deeper issues such as loneliness, grief, or fear.
teaches: “Godliness with contentment is great gain” (1 Timothy 6:6). “I have learned to be content regardless of my circumstances.” “Set your minds on things above, not on earthly things.” Appearance changes can be fine and helpful, but they cannot fix the heart’s deeper longings. Ask what you hope the change would give you: acceptance, love, safety? God offers those in Christ. And caring for your body is wise.
self_statements: Everything would be better if I looked better.
My problems are because of my looks.
I will be happy after I change.
People would like me if I looked right.
This one thing holds me back.
errors: Believing a change would fix everything or nothing would.
Feeling insecure and concluding that appearance is the cause.
questions: What do I hope would change if my looks changed?
Which of those could I seek now?
What has changed before, and did it solve things?
What do I need more than a new look: acceptance, friendship, peace?
What does Scripture say about contentment?
Who could help me look at the deeper issue?
truth: My life will not be fixed by a different look. The deeper longings for love, acceptance, and peace are met in God and in healthy relationships. I can care for my appearance without making it my savior.
hw_truths: Godliness with contentment is great gain.
I can set my mind on higher things.
The deeper needs are met in God.
I am fearfully and wonderfully made.
I can seek help for deeper issues.
log: Each week, note one deeper need and one way you met it.
actions: Write what you want a change to give you.
Take a step toward that need.
prayer: Lord, I think a new look would fix me. Teach me contentment, meet my deeper needs, and help me care for myself without making appearance my hope. Amen.
